raw_corpus_excerpt:
Title: Machine-Learning Sepsis Early Warning Systems in Adult ICUs: A Synthetic PRISMA 2020 Systematic Re
view
Authors: Priya Nair, MD; Lukas Meyer, PhD; Mei-Ling Zhou, MSc
Affiliations: Institute of Critical Care Informatics, Synthetic University Hospital (SYNTHETIC DATA)
Background: Automated sepsis alerts aim to shorten time-to-antibiotics in adult intensive care units, yet
prospective clinical impact remains heterogeneous.
Objectives: Synthesize prospective ICU implementations evaluating mortality, antibiotic timing, and false
-alarm burden under PRISMA 2020 guidelines.
Methods: MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and IEEE Xplore were searched through June 2026 (PROSPERO CRD
42026000999-SYN). Risk of bias was assessed via ROBINS-I and RoB 2.
Results: Of 3,420 records identified (610 duplicates removed), 2,810 titles/abstracts were screened, 2,66
4 excluded, 146 full texts assessed, 128 excluded, and 18 prospective studies (N = 94,300 ICU admissions; 6 RCTs, 12 interventional cohorts) were included.
Waveform+EHR multimodal models achieved median AUROC 0.87 (IQR 0.84-0.90) vs 0.78 (0.74-0.81) for vitals-
only alerts, reducing median time-to-antimicrobials by 1.8 hours.
Limitations: High alert fatigue in uncalibrated thresholds; heterogeneous Sepsis-3 adjudication across si
tes.
Conclusions: Prospective ICU sepsis warning systems consistently accelerate antimicrobial delivery, while
mortality benefit clusters in studies pairing human nurse-physician workflow integration.
